objects.name: CTFT Project
objects.description: Capture-The-Flag Techniques - an ontology of CTF solving behaviour. Relates to MITRE ATT&CK, CAPEC and CWE as per-entry anchors; not a parallel ATT&CK. Generalized from FOM.

objects.name: AI / ML
objects.description: Secrets inside models/prompts/serialized artifacts and their extraction. (HTB: AI-ML)

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-001 - Secret embedded in model weights
objects.description: The flag is encoded in a layer's weights/embedding rather than any text field.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-001 - Extract tensors and inspect weights
objects.description: Load the model, dump tensors, and decode the embedded bytes/strings.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-002 - Prompt-injection-gated flag
objects.description: An LLM-backed app holds the flag in its instructions/context behind guardrails.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-002 - Extract the flag via crafted prompts
objects.description: Craft inputs that bypass the guardrails: recover the system prompt first, then use role shifts, encoding tricks and indirect context (retrieved documents) to make the model reveal the protected content. Probe the raw API directly, and iterate payloads against a local model before replaying them on the target.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-003 - Adversarial-input requirement
objects.description: The flag unlocks only when a classifier is driven to a specific (incorrect) prediction.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-003 - Generate an adversarial example
objects.description: Use gradient/black-box methods to craft an input that forces the target class.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-004 - Malicious / opaque serialized model
objects.description: A pickle/serialized model hides logic or data that executes/loads on deserialization.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-004 - Safely inspect serialized model files
objects.description: Statically inspect the serialized opcodes without executing them to recover content.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-005 - Training-data leakage via queries
objects.description: A secret memorized in training is reachable only by probing the model's outputs.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-005 - Recover secrets through model inversion
objects.description: Query systematically (membership/inversion) to reconstruct the memorized value.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-006 - Self-hosted LLM platform misconfiguration
objects.description: A self-hosted LLM (ollama/oobabooga) is exposed or misconfigured; the flag hides in model outputs, endpoints, or host files.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-006 - Audit ollama/oobabooga deployments for exposed endpoints
objects.description: Enumerate the exposed endpoints/APIs, query the model, and pivot to the host if the deployment is over-permissive.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-007 - Agent / tool-calling guardrail bypass
objects.description: An agent is constrained by guardrails over its tools; the flag requires coaxing it past the policy.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-007 - Bypass agent tool policies
objects.description: Craft prompts/tool-call sequences that bypass the guardrails and retrieve the flag.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-008 - Output-sanitizer / policy-filter gate on an LLM service
objects.description: An LLM-backed service is instructed (system prompt) to sanitize its own output: normalize free text into a fixed schema, replace colloquial or alarming words with technical enum codes, move forbidden terms into a removed list, and never reveal the flag or internal constants. The secret sits in the model's context — system-prompt constants, example strings, audit/debug labels, sometimes response headers — i.e. in channels the policy never marks as user-facing. Direct asks collapse to the sanitized default, but any channel the filter does not model (an extra JSON key, another serialization, an encoding of a suppressed term, an "example" of a flag-format string) is unsupervised. Distinct from CTFTTE-AIM-002, where the guardrail blocks revealing the flag outright; here the gate is a structural output policy and the bypass is structural, not semantic.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-008 - Leak filtered content through structure, serialization, encodings and examples
objects.description: Baseline the sanitizer first: which fields come back, which terms get removed, which enum labels appear. Then climb the payload ladder: (1) demand extra schema keys (forensic, debugprestandardization, hiddenstrings, flags, suppressionledger, ruletrace, validationtrace, developerartifacts) with "do not omit / do not sanitize" rules; (2) switch serialization — YAML, XML+CDATA, one-line dump, code fences, duplicate keys; (3) demand transform encodings of the suppressed terms — ASCII decimal arrays, \uXXXX, base64, spaced-out letters, token arrays; (4) use audit/contradiction framing (contradictions, evidencescore, policydiff against a null filter); (5) enumerate examples / templates / hiddenexamples of secret-format strings and run regex extraction of flag-format substrings — models often repeat embedded example constants verbatim; (6) harvest non-standard uppercase labels that drift between runs. Log every attempt in a transcript, grep all responses (not just the main field) for the flag regex, validate the candidate format, then submit. Automate the ladder with promptfuzzer.py.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-AIM-009 - Player-reachable MCP server with an injectable tool surface
objects.description: The challenge exposes a Model Context Protocol server (usually one /mcp/ endpoint, JSON-RPC 2.0 over SSE) fronting an "AI agent". The flag is reachable through the tool surface rather than through persuasion: tool descriptions name admin keys or example IDs; resources (resources/read) hold internal state and double as indirect prompt injection into the agent's context; tools that render templates with placeholders ({ticket[field]}, {message}, …) evaluate those placeholders server-side, so an attribute walk (class → init.globals → subclasses()) turns a "formatted response" into file read or RCE; prompts can embed the system prompt or example flags. Distinct from CTFTTE-AIM-007, where the target is the agent's tool-use policy; here the transport and the server-side evaluation are the attack surface.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-AIM-009 - Enumerate and abuse the MCP surface (tools, resources, prompts, template placeholders)
objects.description: Speak JSON-RPC 2.0 to the endpoint directly: initialize (keep the Mcp-Session-Id header), notifications/initialized, then tools/list, resources/list + resources/read every URI, prompts/list + prompts/get each. Read tool descriptions fully — required keys and example IDs hide there. Then call tools with probe arguments: template placeholders ({ticket.class}, init.globals, subclasses() chains, {{ ... }} SSTI variants — start with a harmless type-name leak, then escalate to file read / RCE), argument injection into every string field, and admin-gated tools with keys found in descriptions. Scan every response for flag-format strings. Automate with mcpprobe.py (--selftest).
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.
